messages.content: Explain the difference between weather and climate. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Weather refers to the day-to-day conditions of the atmosphere, such as temperature, rain, and wind, at a specific time and place. In contrast, climate is the average of these weather patterns over a much longer period, usually thirty years or more. A simple way to remember the difference is that weather tells you what to wear today, while climate tells you what types of clothes to buy.
